question: Do different laboratories get the same result from the same sample?

broothaerts2020.cite: Broothaerts et al. (2020). Ten years of proficiency testing reveals an improvement in the analytical performance of EU National Reference Laboratories for genetically modified food and feed. Food Control 114: 107237.
broothaerts2020.checked: every quote read word for word in the open-access full text from Europe PMC (PMC7224516, full-text XML) on 20 Nov 2026; places are the article's numbered sections; reference numbers are left out of the quotes

steps.title: Prepare identical items
steps.text: A coordinator makes test items that are the same for everyone and ships them to each laboratory.

quotes.text: For each PT round two test items were prepared and distributed to the participants, consisting of a food or feed matrix containing or spiked with one or more GMOs.

steps.title: Labs measure
steps.text: Each laboratory analyses its item with its usual method, without knowing the answer, and reports the result.

quotes.text: received the test items together with the instruction to identify the unknown GM event(s) present in the materials and to quantify the event(s) identified.

steps.title: Set the target
steps.text: Fix the value the results are judged against: from how the item was made, from expert laboratories, from a certified reference, or from a robust mean of all results.

quotes.text: (i) from the formulation (mass fraction), (ii) by consensus of results reported by expert laboratories (using real-time or digital PCR), (iii) using the certified value of a certified reference material (CRM), or (iv) by calculating the robust mean of the results reported by the NRLs.
quotes.where: section 2.2, ways of setting the assigned value

steps.title: Score each lab
steps.text: Compare each result with the target and score it. A lab with an unsatisfactory score looks for the cause.

quotes.text: The results reported by the NRLs were then compared to the assigned values and scored by using the percentage deviation
NRLs that obtained an unsatisfactory z score were requested to perform a root-cause analysis

steps.title: Read the spread
steps.text: The spread of all the labs' results shows how reproducible the method is between laboratories; repeated rounds show whether it improves.

quotes.text: The outcome revealed a gradual decrease of the relative standard deviation within the sets of the reported data with time.

limits: The card's defining reference, the IUPAC International Harmonized Protocol (Thompson et al. 2006), could not be read: the publisher's page answered with a bot check. The page follows one proficiency-testing scheme, Broothaerts et al. (2020), instead.
The z-score formula and the homogeneity test of ISO 13528 and the IUPAC protocol are not shown, because neither text was read.
